item.title: Differentiable and Constrained Model Predictive Control on the GPU
item.description: In this work, we introduce a differentiable, GPU-accelerated, nonlinear MPC framework that can handle state and input constraints via the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). The method builds on a sequential quadratic programming (SQP) formulation and leverages GPU-optimized linear system solvers for scalability. We demonstrate our approach on drone obstacle avoidance, reinforcement learning, and humanoid imitation learning tasks.

item.title: End-to-End Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for High-Rate FPGA-Accelerated Model Predictive Control on Tiny Drones
item.description: Our system features a solver based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) framework, tailored for FPGA implementation using reduced-precision arithmetic, paired with a custom-designed lightweight, 6g PCB to ensure high-bandwidth communication for deployment on a 35g Crazyflie quadrotor. This tight hardware-algorithm integration enables 500 Hz constrained control over long horizons, a regime previously unattainable. Hardware experiments demonstrate up to 16× faster solve times and a 244× improvement in energydelay product over state-of-the-art, embedded, microcontrollerbased solvers, proving that co-design is essential for sophisticated constrained control on highly compute-limited platforms.
